v1_entries: DATA-SOURCES-v1.json (unchanged; every v1 value is still used when the corresponding v1.1 mode is off)
verification_note: Bibliographic data checked through Crossref or the publisher record; numeric values taken from the documents named per entry. Where only an abstract or an index record could be read, the entry says so.

pichler2020.cite: P. Pichler, B. J. Simonds, J. W. Sowards, G. Pottlacher, Measurements of thermophysical properties of solid and liquid NIST SRM 316L stainless steel, J. Mater. Sci. 55 (2020) 4081-4093, doi 10.1007/s10853-019-04261-6 (open access; read through PMC8193647)
pichler2020.material: NIST SRM 1155a (mass %: Fe 64.71, Cr 17.80, Ni 12.47, Mo 2.19, Mn 1.59, Si 0.52, C 0.026); a Cr-Ni(-Mo) austenitic steel close to 304, not 304
pichler2020.method: ohmic wire pulse heating (about 50 us per experiment), GUM uncertainties at k = 2
pichler2020.note: Table 6 densities lie 18 kg/m3 (0.3 %) below the Table 3 fit at every row; the fit is used, the offset is inside the 3 % uncertainty. The paper reports no thermal conductivity, Lorenz number or emissivity.

sommerfeld_lorenz.use: Wiedemann-Franz thermal conductivity of the liquid
sommerfeld_lorenz.note: the TU Graz group uses L = 2.45e-8 V^2/K^2 (Wilthan, Schuetzenhoefer, Pottlacher, Int. J. Thermophys. 36 (2015) 2259, metadata verified through Crossref; the value from the indexed abstract, full text not accessed); the difference is 0.3 %

janaf_extra.cite: NIST-JANAF tables Mn-003 Mn(l), Mn-005 Mn(g), Si-003 Si(l), Si-005 Si(g), C-002 C(ref = graphite), C-003 C(g)
janaf_extra.check: the vapor law gives 1 bar at the JANAF normal boiling points of Fe, Cr, Ni, Mn and Si within 2.2e-5 decades

zellars1960.cite: G. R. Zellars, S. L. Payne, J. P. Morris, R. L. Kipp, The activities of iron and nickel in liquid Fe-Ni alloys, AIME Iron and Steel Division (1960) (abstract read on onemine.org)
zellars1960.value: activity coefficients at infinite dilution at 1600 C: 0.40 for Fe, 0.66 for Ni; Fe ideal down to mole fraction 0.7; Knudsen vapor-pressure method

gilby1969.cite: S. W. Gilby, G. R. St. Pierre, Equilibrium vapor compositions and activities of components for Fe-Cr-Ni alloys at 1600 C, AIME (1969/1970) (abstract read on onemine.org)
gilby1969.value: in iron-rich alloys the interactions between the three components are negligible

roy1965.cite: P. Roy, R. Hultgren, Vapor-pressure studies of iron-manganese alloys, AIME Institute of Metals Division (1965) (abstract read on onemine.org)
roy1965.value: Fe-Mn solutions nearly ideal (solid alloys, 1250-1500 K); torsion values up to 50 % above Knudsen values attributed to surface depletion of Mn

knight1979.cite: C. J. Knight, Theoretical modeling of rapid surface vaporization with back pressure, AIAA J. 17 (1979) 519-523
knight1979.via: jump conditions as reproduced in M. Schreter-Fleischhacker et al., arXiv:2501.18781 (2025), Appendix D, Eq. D.1-D.3 and the sonic values p = 0.206 p_sat, rho = 0.308 rho_sat (pdf sha256 aa4fccdd7380acc0cde663b10b2077f74abfb0a285afc234cfc73470a939ee8f)
knight1979.check: M = 1: T_v/T_s 0.6691, rho 0.3081, p 0.2062, net flux 0.8157 of the one-sided flux, recoil 0.5498 p_sat

cezairliyan1980.cite: A. Cezairliyan, A. P. Miiller, Thermophysical measurements on low carbon 304 stainless steel above 1400 K by a transient (subsecond) technique, Int. J. Thermophys. 1 (1980) 83-95, doi 10.1007/BF00506274 (metadata through Crossref; values from the abstract as indexed, full text not accessed)
cezairliyan1980.value: hemispherical total emittance 0.37 (5 %); melting point 1707 K; normal spectral emittance 0.385 at 653 nm at melting
cezairliyan1980.note: the indexed abstract text did not let the temperature range of the 0.37 value be resolved between the 1400-1700 K measurement range and a stated 1700-1900 K; it is used for solid and liquid alike

roger1979.cite: C. R. Roger, S. H. Yen, K. G. Ramanathan, Temperature variation of total hemispherical emissivity of stainless steel AISI 304, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 69 (1979) 1384-1390
roger1979.use: not used numerically (340-1100 K, polished samples); cited for the low-temperature behaviour

mills2004_melt.cite: Mills et al. 2004 (see v1): surface tension Eq. 23 and 26 (S dependence), dgamma/dT Eq. 27, viscosity Eq. 28 ln eta(mPa s) = -2.396 + 7950/T (Brooks, oscillation viscometry on a 25.6Cr-6.5Ni-4Mo steel, about 1773-1900 K), Table 3(b) 8.07 / 7.54 / 5.98 mPa s at 1773 / 1800 / 1900 K
mills2004_melt.uncertainty: surface tension 3 %; viscosity of the order of 10 % for pure metals, commercial alloys more variable (Mills Sec. 8)

miotello1995.cite: A. Miotello, R. Kelly, Critical assessment of thermal models for laser sputtering at high fluences, Appl. Phys. Lett. 67 (1995) 3535, doi 10.1063/1.114912 (abstract through Crossref)
miotello1995.use: phase explosion (explosive boiling) as the thermal mechanism of high-fluence ablation
miotello1995.note: the onset at 0.9 T_c used here is the conventional approximation named in the requirement; the factor was not verified from a source and is configurable

critical_points.cite: Sjostrom 2023 (304L EOS, 9500 K, 0.615 GPa, 1.1 g/cm3); Mattsson & Desjarlais 2004 (steel QMD, 10000 K at 2 g/cc, about 2000 K above SESAME 4272)
critical_points.use: T_c = 8000 K (lowest estimate) gives the phase-explosion temperature 7200 K, above the 6000 K law domain

values.value: h = -335000 + 847 T + h_v1(298.15 K) J/kg for T >= 1727 K; linear in T across 1672-1727 K from the Mills solid value
values.tag: measured (1708-2900 K), model_derived above 2900 K and in the mushy interpolation
values.uncertainty: 2.9 % (k = 2) in range; implied latent heat about 290 kJ/kg (pichler2020) versus 276 kJ/kg (Mills, v1)
4.5 % (k = 2); at 6000 K the linear fit gives 2.29 uOhm m

values.check: 29.4 W/(m K) at 1800 K versus Mills Table 3(b) 29 (10 %)

values.uncertainty: grade allows Mn up to 2 %; foil heat composition unknown

values.value: JANAF gas minus condensed Gibbs energy (Mn and Si: pure liquid; C: graphite)
values.tag: recommended (Mn liquid table to 3000 K, Si to 4500 K, continued with constant Cp above)

values.value: regular solution, Omega_FeNi = R 1873 ln 0.66 = -6470 J/mol; all other pairs 0
values.tag: measured (binary Fe-Ni at 1873 K), model_derived (regular-solution temperature dependence, zero pairs)
values.uncertainty: gilby1969 reports negligible interactions in iron-rich ternary alloys, so gamma_Ni lies between 0.71 (this model at x_Ni = 0.09) and 1; Si and C activity coefficients not acquired (gamma = 1 is an upper bound for their tiny fluxes); Mo, P, S not tracked

values.value: E_int,i(T) = m_i h(T) + dHvap_i,JANAF(T)/N_A - 5/2 kT - eps0_i, eps0_i the minimum over the domain
values.tag: model_derived (exact JANAF latent heat at every row; carries gas electronic excitation and the element-versus-alloy caloric difference)
values.uncertainty: partial excess enthalpies of the solution are not included (regular-solution value RT ln gamma, about 3 % of the Ni latent heat)

values.value: Mach number such that the Knudsen-layer pressure equals the patch back pressure (sonic for lower back pressure, no evaporation at or above saturation); net flux and recoil from Knight's relations; same net fraction for every element
values.uncertainty: single-species monatomic jump conditions applied to the mixture; back pressure is the coupling input (native neutral/plasma pressure at the surface)

values.value: 0.37 for solid and liquid; T_env 300 K
values.tag: measured (abstract value), model_derived outside the measured range

values.value: Mills Eq. 26/27 with S mass % (default 0, Eq. 23), Eq. 28
values.uncertainty: S content of the foil unknown: dgamma/dT changes sign above about 40 ppm S (Mills Fig. 13)

values.value: typed refusal at 0.9 T_c (T_c configurable, default 8000 K)
298.2-6000 K (JANAF gas tables end at 6000 K)
